title: The Grasshopper and the Ants
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: One fine day in winter some Ants were busy drying their store of corn, which had got rather damp during a long spell of rain. Presently up came a Grasshopper and begged them to spare her a few grains, "For," she said, "I'm simply starving."

The Ants stopped work for a moment, though this was against their principles. "May we ask," said they, "what you were doing with yourself all last summer? Why didn't you collect a store of food for the winter?" "The fact is," replied the Grasshopper, "I was so busy singing that I hadn't the time." "If you spent the summer singing," replied the Ants, "you can't do better than spend the winter dancing." And they chuckled and went on with their work.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what are the Ants doing on a fine winter day?
options: Building a new nest for the coming spring
Searching for a Grasshopper to help them
Drying their store of corn, which had gotten damp
Repairing damage from a recent storm

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Grasshopper beg the Ants for?
options: A few grains of corn
A place to sleep for the winter
Directions to a warmer place
Help building her own store of food

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why does the Grasshopper say she needs the corn?
options: Because she promised it to another grasshopper
Because she wants to store it for next winter
Because she is preparing a meal for guests
Because she is simply starving

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do the Ants ask the Grasshopper?
options: Where she planned to spend the winter
What she was doing with herself all last summer
How much corn she actually needed
Who told her where to find their store

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Grasshopper explain how she spent the summer?
options: She was searching for a better place to live
She was helping other grasshoppers with their own stores
She was so busy singing that she hadn't the time to collect food
She was resting after a long illness

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do the Ants suggest the Grasshopper do for the winter?
options: Spend the winter dancing
Spend the winter helping them dry corn
Spend the winter searching harder for food
Spend the winter apologizing to other ants

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why do the Ants bring up what the Grasshopper did last summer?
options: To find out if she has any useful skills to offer them
To decide whether she deserves a larger share than usual
To learn where she has been hiding all winter
To point out that her own choices led directly to her present hunger

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Ants' remark about "dancing" in winter suggest about their attitude toward the Grasshopper's request?
options: They genuinely believe dancing will keep her warm through winter
They are pointing out, with some amusement, that her past choices leave her with no one to blame but herself
They are planning to teach her how to dance in exchange for food
They feel guilty and are looking for a way to help her indirectly

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "principles" mean in "this was against their principles"?
options: Small tools used for measuring
Songs they typically sing while working
Firm rules or standards they normally follow
Debts they owed to other ants

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Failing to prepare during a time of plenty can leave you without help when hard times come
Singing is a waste of time in every season
Ants are always unwilling to share what they have
Grasshoppers are naturally lazier than ants

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why had the Ants' corn gotten damp?
options: A leak in their storage hole
Melting snow from the roof
Water spilled by another animal
A long spell of rain

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do the Ants do briefly when the Grasshopper arrives?
options: They hide their store of corn
They stop work for a moment
They call other ants for a meeting
They offer her a place to sleep

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do the Ants do after giving their reply to the Grasshopper?
options: They invite her to join them permanently
They give her a portion of the corn anyway
They chuckle and go on with their work
They argue among themselves about what to do

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why might stopping work be described as "against their principles"?
options: The Ants generally value steady, uninterrupted labor and rarely pause for anything
The Ants have a strict rule against speaking to grasshoppers
The Ants believe stopping work brings bad luck
The Ants are forbidden from helping any insect during winter

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what contrast does the fable draw between the Ants and the Grasshopper across the seasons?
options: The Ants sang through summer while the Grasshopper worked quietly
Both the Ants and the Grasshopper spent the summer working equally hard
Neither the Ants nor the Grasshopper made any preparations for winter
The Ants worked to prepare for winter while the Grasshopper spent the same time on leisure

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "spare" mean in "begged them to spare her a few grains"?
options: To measure out precisely
To give up or part with something for another's use
To hide away safely
To refuse to share at all

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Grasshopper and Ants share their winter stores equally
The Ants ask the Grasshopper to sing for them in exchange for corn
A Grasshopper who sang all summer instead of working is denied help by Ants who prepared ahead of time
The Grasshopper teaches the Ants a valuable lesson about enjoying life
